title: Size and shape of specular highlights is unexpected
body: ### Tested versions - v4.5.beta.nixpkgs ### System information v4.5.1.stable.nixpkgs [f62fdbde1] ### Issue description The angle and size of specular highlights seems to be kind of weird. It is somewhat visible with "normal" lights ... But it can get really strange if you increase the size of the lamp. Because in general my expectation is that the highlight should look somewhat like the reflection of a sphere - so a sphere. At high roughness values there also is an optical phenomenon where reflections do get very stretched on semi-rough surfaces. My best guess is that this is what the math tries to do but somewhere it went wrong. So this is the setup: the light with a size of 1m (does that mean radius or diameter?) reflected onto a wall and a floor. And while some weirdness is expected when lights intersect a reflecting plane or at very steep angles, the godot behavior is really strange and both eevee and flax do not have these stretching/scaling inconsistencies. | at a low angle | at a high angle | eevee comparison | cycles reference | | --- | --- | --- | --- | | | | | | What is interesting when you compare eevee against cycles is: cycles also slightly has this taper out towards the top of the reflection that godot does. I think the godot implementation is on the right track, but has some math errors that cause it to look very strange as of now. And just to avoid the controversy that messed up the first attempt at me reporting this issue: I am adding the lampshades so you can get a better intuitive understanding of the omnilight/point light size. They are otherwise just lamp shades with an inverted hull that do not interact with the lighting. ### Steps to reproduce 1. add a lamp 2. add a mesh plane 3. move the lamp above the mesh plane 4. add a material to the mesh plane and set its roughness to something lower than 0.4 (makes it easier to see) 5. increase the size of the lamp (makes it easier to see) 6. rotate around the lamp tilting up and down to see if it looks plausible ### Minimal reproduction project (MRP) n/a
